task_production_rates.name: Inspect Wall Surface

QT2.notes: Quick walk-through, major defects only. Minimal time investment.

QT3.notes: Standard inspection with raking work light. Identify and mark all visible defects.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive inspection under bright raking light. Mark all imperfections systematically.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of wall surfaces with raking work light. Wall inspection is faster than ceiling (~1500 vs ~1250 SF/hr at QT3) because viewing angle is natural and lighting is easier to position. QT2 rate (2000 SF/hr) is 33% faster than QT3 because: (1) ambient light only, no raking light setup, (2) only flagging major obvious defects, (3) no marking of minor ridges/dimples. QT4 rate (1000 SF/hr) is 33% slower due to comprehensive systematic scan.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Only major defects noted — unfilled joints, holes, exposed fasteners
defect_tolerance.QT3: All visible defects at 6 feet viewing distance, minor texture variations acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT4: All imperfections visible at 3 feet under raking light, texture inconsistencies flagged

task_production_rates.name: Repair Wall Defects

QT2.notes: Fill major defects only. Quick spackle, minimal sanding.

QT3.notes: Fill all marked defects, sand smooth, feather edges. New construction Good condition = moderate defect count.

QT4.notes: Thorough repair of all defects. Meticulous feathering, uniform surface. More time per repair.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Rate expressed per SF of wall area, not per defect. New construction Good condition means lower defect density — rate reflects time to walk, find, and fill defects across the wall area. Includes spackle + sand time. QT2 rate (1500 SF/hr) is 87% faster than QT3 (800 SF/hr) because: (1) only major defects filled (holes, unfilled joints), (2) minor ridges/dimples left as-is, (3) less time spent on feathering and finishing. QT4 rate (500 SF/hr) is 37% slower due to thorough repair of all defects with meticulous feathering.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Major defects filled. Minor ridges and dimples left.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All marked defects filled and sanded smooth. Minor imperfections acceptable if not visible at 6 feet.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired to flat, smooth surface. No visible ridges or dimples at 3 feet under raking light.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Wall Drywall Dust
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment on wall surfaces. Top-to-bottom systematic passes. Walls are faster than ceiling (~800 vs ~700 SF/hr) — natural working position, no overhead reach.

defect_tolerance.all: All surfaces dust-free. No visible dust on hand wipe test.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Position canvas drop cloths along base of walls. Perimeter drops are faster than full-room coverage — no taping seams, just unroll and position.

defect_tolerance.all: Drops positioned along all walls being worked. No gaps at corners. Floor visible only in center of room.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown (Perimeter)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fold and remove perimeter drops. Faster than setup — just gather and fold.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Full Room)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Full room floor coverage with rosin paper or plastic. Tape seams. Same rate as ceiling floor protection setup — floor protection scope is identical regardless of whether spray target is walls or ceiling.

defect_tolerance.all: Full room coverage, all seams taped, perimeter taped, no gaps or exposed floor.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown (Full Room)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fold and remove floor protection. Faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Outlet Covers, Switch Plates, and HVAC Registers

heuristic.notes: Per-room heuristic — average 6 outlets/switches per room. Includes removal of outlet covers, switch plates, and any HVAC register covers in the room.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Per-room rate using heuristic of ~6 outlets/switches per room. At ~2 min per removal = ~12 min per room = ~5 rooms/hr. Faster than masking and produces a cleaner result.

defect_tolerance.all: All covers and registers removed and labeled. No damage to covers or wall surface.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Electrical Boxes and Light Fixtures

heuristic.notes: Per-room heuristic — same room count as cover removal. Masking exposed boxes (~6 per room) plus any light fixtures in the room.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Per-room rate using heuristic of ~6 boxes per room plus light fixtures. At ~3 min per item = ~20 min per room = ~3 rooms/hr.

defect_tolerance.all: All electrical boxes fully masked. Light fixtures loosened and wrapped. No exposed surfaces in overspray zone.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Masking from Boxes and Fixtures

heuristic.notes: Per-room heuristic — same room count. Removing masking is faster than applying it.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Per-room rate. Removing masking and re-seating light fixtures. Faster than setup — just pull tape and push fixtures back. ~12 min per room. Covers and registers are NOT reinstalled during prime phase.

defect_tolerance.all: All masking removed. Light fixtures re-seated flush. No tape residue.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge

QT2.notes: Acceptable edge, coverage is priority over line quality.

QT3.notes: Clean, consistent edge. No visible wobble at 6 feet distance.

QT4.notes: Crisp edge with minimal brush marks. Straight line, no visible wobble at 3 feet.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Freehand brush cut-in at ceiling line from wall perspective. Wall cut-in at ceiling is faster than ceiling cut-in at wall (~100 vs ~85 LF/hr at QT3) — working at comfortable height, not overhead. Height modifier applies for tall/high/extreme walls. QT2 rate (125 LF/hr) is 25% faster than QT3 (100 LF/hr) because: (1) coverage is priority over line quality, (2) minor edge wobble acceptable, (3) less time spent on precision. QT4 rate (75 LF/hr) is 25% slower due to crisp edge requirement with no visible wobble.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible wobble acceptable if coverage is complete. No bare spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Reasonably straight line, minor wobble acceptable only at distance (6+ feet)
defect_tolerance.QT4: Clean line, no visible wobble at 3 feet, minimal brush marks

task_production_rates.name: Roll Primer on Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Single journeyman, 9-inch roller on extension pole, smooth wall. Wall rolling is the baseline — ceiling rolling (~300 SF/hr) is ~14% slower due to overhead fatigue.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any tier. Surface uniformly sealed. Properly painted surface per PCA.

task_production_rates.name: Roll Primer on Wall (Textured Surface)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Textured wall surface with 3/4-inch nap roller. Texture slows application — heavier nap, more product, work primer into valleys. Ceiling textured rolling (~235 SF/hr) is ~15% slower.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. All texture valleys filled and sealed.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Primer on Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray at proper mil thickness on walls. Wall spray is the baseline — ceiling spray (~500 SF/hr) is ~17% slower due to overhead position. In spray+backroll system, spray rate is coupled to backroll rate (spray cannot exceed backroll).

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any tier. Uniform mil thickness.

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Sprayed Wall Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 18-inch roller on extension pole immediately following spray. Wall backroll is the baseline — ceiling backroll (~325 SF/hr) is ~19% slower due to overhead fatigue. This is the bottleneck rate in spray+backroll system.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Primer fully consolidated into drywall. No air pockets or stipple.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge After Wall Spray

QT2.notes: Quick touch-up only where spray overshot ceiling line.

QT3.notes: Clean edge, cover any spray overshoot at ceiling line.

QT4.notes: Crisp edge, straight line, no visible overshoot.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up cut-in at ceiling line after spray/backroll. Faster than primary cut-in because only addressing spray overshoot areas, not full-length cut. QT2 rate (150 LF/hr) is 25% faster than QT3 (120 LF/hr) because: (1) quick touch-up only where spray overshot, (2) less precision required, (3) minor imperfections acceptable. QT4 rate (90 LF/hr) is 25% slower due to crisp edge requirement.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Primer line at ceiling covered. Minor imperfection acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean edge, no visible overshoot at 6 feet
defect_tolerance.QT4: Crisp edge, straight line, no visible overshoot at 3 feet

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Floor After Wall Prime
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Quick vacuum of floor area to remove debris. Fast task — just sweeping/vacuuming floor, not detailed surface cleaning.

defect_tolerance.all: Floor area clean and free of visible debris.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time task — clean brushes, rollers, spray equipment with water. Not driven by wall area. 20 minutes is typical for single-product cleanup.

defect_tolerance.all: All tools cleaned. No dried primer on reusable equipment.

task_production_rates.name: Final Wall Inspection

QT2.notes: Quick visual scan for major misses.

QT3.notes: Walk all surfaces with raking light, touch up as needed.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive inspection under raking light, touch up any visible defects.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of completed wall primer. Wall final inspection is faster than ceiling (~2000 vs ~1750 SF/hr at QT3) — natural viewing angle. QT2 rate (3000 SF/hr) is 50% faster than QT3 (2000 SF/hr) because: (1) quick visual scan only, (2) ambient light, no raking light, (3) only checking for major misses. Still catches drips, sags, and holidays. QT4 rate (1200 SF/hr) is 40% slower due to comprehensive inspection with raking light.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No major holidays or misses. Minor imperfections acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No holidays, drips, or lap marks visible at 6 feet. Touch up any found.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No holidays, drips, lap marks, or edge issues visible at 3 feet under raking light.

quality_tier_effects.description: Minimal wall prime — reduced inspection/repair, basic coverage
quality_tier_effects.notes: Economy work: quick inspection, minimal repair, coverage-only application. Per Modifier_Registry.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard wall prime — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard new construction: proper inspection/repair, single coat, clean edges. Per Modifier_Registry.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium wall prime — thorough inspection/repair, careful application, crisp edges
quality_tier_effects.notes: Premium work: comprehensive inspection, thorough repair, straight edges. Per Modifier_Registry.

height_effects.notes: Baseline — work from floor with extension pole. Standard residential wall height.
Step ladder needed for upper cut-in and rolling. Longer extension pole. Per Modifier_Registry.
Scaffold or baker staging required. Significant access challenge. Per Modifier_Registry.
Scaffold or lift required. 18ft ceiling = 18ft walls. Production rate cuts in half. Per Modifier_Registry and brief Section 9.

texture_effects.notes: Baseline — smooth Level 4 drywall wall. Per Modifier_Registry.
Orange peel texture increases application time ~10%. Per Modifier_Registry.
Knockdown texture increases application time ~15%. Per Modifier_Registry.

drywall_level_effects.notes: Level 3 has more exposed paper, higher absorption, slightly slower application.
Level 5 is uniform surface, slightly better coverage, but may require sand after prime.

coupling_constraints.description: When using spray+backroll on walls, spray rate must not exceed backroll rate. Backroller sets the pace.
coupling_constraints.practical_implication: Wall spray at 600 SF/hr, wall backroll at 400 SF/hr means effective system rate is 400 SF/hr per crew. Spray is coupled to backroll.
coupling_constraints.notes: Per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine § Spray/Backroll Throughput Coupling. Spray and backroll done by 2-person crew working in tandem.

crew_configurations.name: Single Wall Roller
crew_configurations.notes: One person does wall cut-in and rolling with extension pole.

crew_configurations.name: Wall Roller Pair
crew_configurations.notes: Cutter stays ahead of roller for larger wall areas. Maintains wet edge.

crew_configurations.name: Wall Spray + Backroll Crew
crew_configurations.notes: Sprayer and backroller work in tandem. Backroller sets pace. Standard NC production crew.

assumptions.value: Wall rates are 14-19% faster than ceiling equivalents across all task types
assumptions.source: Research notes, sibling spec SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME production.json
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifies exact wall/ceiling differential — derived from research on overhead fatigue factor. Field calibration needed.

assumptions.value: Per-room heuristic: avg 6 fixtures/room. Removal ~5 rooms/hr, masking ~3 rooms/hr, unmasking ~5 rooms/hr
assumptions.source: Stakeholder directive — per-room heuristic because individual fixture counting is impractical on job sites
assumptions.note: Uses PS_META.EA.ROOMS_TOTAL as driver. Average 6 outlets/switches per room (range 3-10). Field calibration needed for room average.

risks.description: Height modifier compounds with QT modifier. Extreme height (2.0) + QT4 (1.3) = 2.6x base time. Verify total stacked modifier stays under 4.0 sanity threshold per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine.
risks.mitigation: Flag projects with stacked modifier > 4.0 for review.

risks.description: Substrate repair rates are highly variable depending on drywall contractor quality. Good NC drywall may need almost no repair; poor drywall finish quality could significantly increase repair time.
risks.mitigation: Rate ranges are wide. App allows per-task rate adjustment.

validation_plan.validation_method: Time 3+ jobs with single roller on smooth walls at QT3. Record SF and elapsed time.
Time spray+backroll jobs. Record SF and elapsed time for backroller specifically.
Time ceiling-line cut-in on standard height walls. Record LF and elapsed time.
Time cover/register removal on 3+ jobs. Record count and elapsed time.

research_corrections.title: Spray-only is never valid for priming bare drywall
research_corrections.impact: Removed TSK_WALL_SPRAY_PRIMER_ONLY, TSK_WALL_CUT_IN_CEILING_SPRAY_ONLY rates and CREW_WALL_SPRAY_SINGLE config. application_method reduced to roll and spray_backroll only.
